November is National Family Caregivers Month! Across our communities, family caregivers give their time, energy and love to care for parents, spouses, children and neighbors. Family caregivers keep loved ones safe, help them follow the doctor’s care plan and stay on top of medications, bills and appointments. It’s a full-time job and I am proud to honor these selfless caregivers. 

The work is not easy and the love that family caregivers show every day makes a real difference. Thank you for everything you do!

I’m honored to receive the General Patton Award at the annual Veterans Day event in Chiriaco Summit.  

While I’m grateful to receive this award, the true heroes are the servicemembers who put on the uniform and fight for our country. They answered the call and I’m committed to making sure Congress keeps the promise it made to every one of them when they enlisted. I will always fight for our veterans.  

Thank you for this recognition and thank you to all who served and to the families who served alongside them.

VICTORY! Today the House passed the Major Richard Star Act, my bipartisan bill to ensure combat-injured veterans receive their full retirement and disability benefits.

Thank you to @repmarktakano, and every member who signed our discharge petition to force this vote.

Most https://t.co/Qt3rvHdUEG

Tuesday, I spoke with @Axios about my efforts to fight back against Trump’s cuts to health care. Thank you to everyone who joined us, especially Andrew Solander who led the conversation. 

From prescription drugs to hospital bills, I’ve seen firsthand how rising healthcare costs hurt patients and their families. We know solutions exist. It starts with listening, working together, and having conversations like this one. 

Credit: Denny Henry for Axios

I’m proud to continue highlighting veterans from my district who have served our country. Join me in celebrating Raymond Gonzalez, a U.S. Army 63B veteran who served from 2003 to 2014 before being injured in combat and having to retire. 

Since returning home, Raymond has started https://t.co/qsUwFYMTT6

I’m proud to highlight Dr. Jerry Turner, a disabled U.S. Marine Corps 6842 veteran who served our country during the Gulf War from 1987 to 1993. Dr. Turner answered the call to serve and now he lives with the injuries that came with it. I’m pleased to report that Dr. Turner receives the full VA disability compensation he earned. 

Not every veteran in his family is treated the same way. Dr. Turner is married to a disabled, retired U.S. Navy veteran who completed a full military career and retired honorably, yet his retirement pay was reduced because of the injuries he sustained in service. Two disabled veterans can carry comparable injuries, and the one who served a full career is penalized for it. That is wrong. 

Retirement pay reflects years of service and disability benefits reflect injury — they should never cancel each other out. Dr. Turner’s story is why the Major Richard Star Act is so important. 

Thank you for your service!

I’m proud to continue highlighting veterans from my district who have served our country. Join me in celebrating Raymond Gonzales, a U.S. Army 63B veteran who served from 2003 to 2014 before being injured in combat and having to retire. 

Since returning home, Raymond has started a family, built a small woodworking business, and stayed committed to his fellow veterans, serving on the Imperial County Veterans Advisory Council and the Brawley Elks Lodge Veterans Committee and as an officer with the VFW. 

Veterans, like Raymond, who were injured in combat have earned their retirement and their disability benefits, and I’ll keep fighting to pass the Major Richard Star Act so that they get both. 

Thank you for your service, Raymond.

In celebration of Veteran’s Day, I’m spotlighting veterans from my district. Today, I’m honored to celebrate U.S. Army 13D veteran Daniel Hinojosa Jr. Daniel is a combat veteran who served from 2002 to 2011 and was deployed to Iraq multiple times.  

Daniel was medically retired after sustaining combat-related injuries, and the transition home was not easy. Today, he’s pursuing a Master of Social Work so he can support other veterans in our communities. 

Like thousands of others, Daniel had to choose between his VA disability compensation and his military retirement pay. That’s why I co-authored the Major Richard Star Act, to ensure veterans like Daniel get all the benefits they deserve.  

Thank you for your service, Daniel.

Today, I pause to honor those who answered the call to serve our nation. Their courage, sacrifice and commitment protects the freedoms we cherish every day. To every veteran across our community and our country, thank you.  

I will keep working to ensure that those who served https://t.co/788LzojfbF

post.text:
I’m proud to highlight Dr. Jerry Turner, a disabled U.S. Marine Corps 6842 veteran who served our country during the Gulf War from 1987 to 1993. Dr. Turner answered the call to serve and now he lives with the injuries that came with it. I’m pleased to report that Dr. Turner receives the full VA disability compensation he earned. 

Not every veteran in his family is treated the same way. Dr. Turner is married to a disabled, retired U.S. Navy veteran who completed a full military career and retired honorably, yet his retirement pay was reduced because of the injuries he sustained in service. Two disabled veterans can carry comparable injuries, and the one who served a full career is penalized for it. That is wrong. 

Retirement pay reflects years of service and disability benefits reflect injury — they should never cancel each other out. Dr. Turner’s story is why the Major Richard Star Act is so important. 

Thank you for your service!

I’m proud to continue highlighting veterans from my district who have served our country. Join me in celebrating Raymond Gonzales, a U.S. Army 63B veteran who served from 2003 to 2014 before being injured in combat and having to retire. 

Since returning home, Raymond has started a family, built a small woodworking business, and stayed committed to his fellow veterans, serving on the Imperial County Veterans Advisory Council and the Brawley Elks Lodge Veterans Committee and as an officer with the VFW. 

Veterans, like Raymond, who were injured in combat have earned their retirement and their disability benefits, and I’ll keep fighting to pass the Major Richard Star Act so that they get both. 

Thank you for your service, Raymond.

In celebration of Veteran’s Day, I’m spotlighting veterans from my district. Today, I’m honored to celebrate U.S. Army 13D veteran Daniel Hinojosa Jr. Daniel is a combat veteran who served from 2002 to 2011 and was deployed to Iraq multiple times.  

Daniel was medically retired after sustaining combat-related injuries, and the transition home was not easy. Today, he’s pursuing a Master of Social Work so he can support other veterans in our communities. 

Like thousands of others, Daniel had to choose between his VA disability compensation and his military retirement pay. That’s why I co-authored the Major Richard Star Act, to ensure veterans like Daniel get all the benefits they deserve.  

Thank you for your service, Daniel.

post.text:
Don't forget to set your clocks back! Daylight Saving Time ends this Sunday, November 1.  

As a physician, I know changing the clocks twice a year disrupts our circadian rhythm and impacts our sleep health. I voted to pass the bipartisan Sunshine Protection Act to stop daylights savings. It passed the House, and I urge the Senate to send it to the President’s desk.
